handWritten.note: Written by hand after the runs, from the phases below; the harness writes everything else (merge() in scripts/cdp-m2-05-handoff.mjs). Each phase records its commit, whether the product tree was clean, and the exe's SHA-256. Corrected on 06/10/2026: forgedInputs gains the c-start folder dialog. Final pass: m2-05-handoff-final.json, where limits[0] is fixed (dba3b03) and the file in use of item 2 is named (b146d51).
handWritten.summary: Complement to m2-05-handoff.json on Muse 1.4.2, in the app's isolated test mode, 2 live turns. All four open points hold on the fixed build (4e08e2a): the model's file tools follow the move; a move whose source cleanup fails after the target received the work leaves both sides byte-identical with an honest message; a move is refused while a turn runs and a send is refused while a move runs, with their reasons; a conflict is refused with no event on either side's files. Two defects found and fixed: a file Git cannot delete made the move report success (8dca438), and the Move action was disabled with no reason while Muse responds (4e08e2a).

items.1 file tools after a move: c-file-tools: after Move to worktree, read_file on docs/item1.txt returned the worktree version (line 2 ONLY-IN-WORKTREE-<token>, absent from Local's file: hashes differ, before and after) and the model answered with that line; write_file wrote item1-written.txt (17 bytes) in the worktree; Local byte-identical, the worktree gained only that file.
items.2 both-sides undo: c-held-tracked: src/app.txt held open in Local (FileShare.Read, no delete); the new worktree received the work (74 events there), then Git failed on 'unable to unlink old src/app.txt'; both sides restored (Local's files, status and index identical; the worktree back to its checkout), 2 snapshot refs kept, held file never written, conversation stays. c-held-untracked (fixed build): notes/local.md held; refused the same way with 'Git could not delete notes/local.md (in use by another program?)'. Before the fix (c-held-untracked-before-fix, a9ffff2): Git only warned and exited 0, the move reported 'Moved 4 changed files and 1 untracked file … This conversation now runs there' while Local still held notes/local.md.
items.3 turn/move lock: c-start and c-file-tools, while the turn waits on its first card: the Move action is disabled with 'Muse is still responding: stop the response before moving this conversation.' and a click calls nothing; a direct handoff_move is refused ('a conversation is still responding in this folder: stop it before moving'); C, idle in Local (A's host folder), asks through the UI: question, OK, new worktree, then the same refusal on screen, no event on Local's files. c-send-during-move, no IPC block: A's composer is disabled with 'This conversation's folder is being moved: send once the move is done.'; C's send through its composer, 463 ms into the move, is refused by the supervisor ('this conversation's folder is being moved: send again once the move is done') while the move still runs, kept as an unsent row; no turn in C.
items.4 conflict before any write: c-conflict: Move back to local with src/app.txt and staged.txt changed on both sides: refused in the UI before the question and by a direct handoff_move; 0 events on Local's files (its 5 folders watched one by one) and in the worktree (recursive) during each refusal; both sides byte-identical, no ref. Git's own .git saw about 1300 events per refusal: existing loose objects freshened by the snapshots, a few new snapshot objects, an index lock.
items.5 earlier record: m2-05-handoff.json: fixes[0].insufficient corrected (dialog:allow-confirm exists in tauri-plugin-dialog 2.7.3 as a deprecated alias of allow-message, already granted); its hand-written fields listed in handWritten.
items.6 SPEC: docs/SPEC.md: the M2-05 paragraph describes handoff_preview and handoff_move instead of the removed buildHandoffPlan.

fixes.defect: Git only warns when it cannot delete a file (on Windows, one another program holds open without delete sharing) and exits 0. A moved untracked file held in the source stayed there while the move reported success and the conversation followed; a deletion the target could not apply was lost on both sides.
fixes.after: handoff_move checks, after writing the target and after cleaning the source, that every file to delete is gone; otherwise the step fails and both sides are restored, the message naming the file. Tests (Windows): handoff_undoes_a_move_that_left_a_moved_file_in_the_source, handoff_undoes_a_move_that_could_not_delete_a_file_in_the_target, both failing without the fix. Live: c-held-untracked-before-fix vs c-held-untracked.

fixes.defect: While Muse responds, the Move action was disabled with no reason (its title only covered remote conversations).
fixes.after: moveBlockedReason (src/lib/handoff.ts) gives the reason, shown as the action's title. Test: handoff.test.ts, failing without the fix. Live: c-start and c-file-tools.

forgedInputs: C was started by a direct start_session (no turn) and adopted on a reload: the host refused A's Fork conversation after a finished turn (MSP -32023 forkBoundaryInvalid WriteFailed, the known upstream Windows defect, docs/upstream). Same in the rehearsal that recorded c-held-untracked-before-fix, where A was started that way too.
The TaskDialog's buttons are pressed with TDM_CLICK_BUTTON, as in the earlier record.

c-start: the welcome screen's folder dialog (plugin:dialog|open) never showed: the harness's IPC interceptor (dialogQueue in scripts/cdp-harness.mjs) answered it with the test repository, as CDP cannot drive the OS folder dialog. The picker, A's first message and Start went through the UI.
Direct native calls only to show refusals: handoff_move while A responds (c-file-tools) and during the conflict (c-conflict).
Held files: a separate PowerShell process opens them with FileShare.Read and no delete sharing, as an editor or viewer does.
limits: A refused or failed move to a new worktree leaves that new, clean worktree and its muse/ branch (listed in the app's worktrees); the message does not mention it (<worktree c>, <worktree 2>, <worktree 3>).

The preview writes one loose object per new untracked file. In the rehearsal, 3000 new files took about 200 s before the question showed; outside the app, 200 new blobs took 13 to 18 s with or without core.fsync on this machine. The move itself took about 7 s for 2000 files (moveSeenRunningMs).

A recursive fs.watch on Local overflows during Git's bursts in .git (libuv reports nameless events, recorded as overflow): item 4 watches Local's folders one by one; item 2's recursive watcher lost none.
The model's shell still reports the folder in the \\?\ form (#88).
